circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the home of Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern venue to host a Grand Prix, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: A street circuit encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, this venue holds an FIA Grade 1 classification and annually hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting motorsport events including the Supercars Championship race.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix across two separate eras: initially from 1970 to 1987 under its original name, then again from 1997 to 2003 following a redesign and shortening of the track.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that measures 6. 003 km per lap, ranking it as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming a regular fixture on the calendar in 2017 under its current Azerbaijan Grand Prix designation.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: The Bahrain International Circuit, which opened in 2004, is a 5. 412 km motorsport facility that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond hosting the annual F1 race, the venue accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 Series competitions and 24-hour endurance events, while maintaining FIA Grade 1 certification with multiple configurable layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it versatile for various racing demands. The FIA Grade 1-licensed facility accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its viewing stands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated near Spa in Belgium's Wallonia region, this 7-kilometer circuit has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix continuously since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006. The venue boasts a storied history in motorsport, having staged a Grand Prix as far back as 1925 and participating in Formula One's inaugural season in 1950.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361-kilometer circuit hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix annually. Beyond Formula One, the track has served as a venue for various international motorsport competitions including sports car racing and American open-wheel racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019 before resuming in 2024. The circuit has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing events alongside its traditional Grand Prix commitments.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English racing venue inaugurated the British Grand Prix in 1948 and later staged the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. Following decades of hosting the British Grand Prix alongside other circuits, it became the permanent home of the event from 1987 onwards and continues to serve as the venue for major international motorsport competitions.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc in 1986. Originally envisioned as a street circuit in Budapest's central park, the venue was instead constructed outside the city in just eight months, making it the fastest-built Formula One track to that date.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Italy's Autodromo Nazionale di Monza, constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility, spans 5. 793 kilometres and serves as the primary venue for the Italian Grand Prix, a fixture on the Formula One calendar since 1949 (excluding 1980 during renovations). The track earns its "Temple of Speed" nickname from its extended straights and fast-flowing corner design, making it one of only four circuits that have appeared consistently in F1 since the championship's inception.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is renowned as a premier destination for Formula One racing and hosts major international motorsport events throughout the year.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course located in Paradise, Nevada that navigates through the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban streets. The track winds past many of the city's iconic destinations, such as the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, incorporating these landmark hotels and casinos into its layout.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City honoring two Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both died in racing accidents during the 1960s. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix from 2015 onwards on its current configuration, having previously held the race on an earlier layout through 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary racing facility constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Built by specialist circuit designers for the 2022 Formula One season, the track has become the home of the Miami Grand Prix and also hosts other major motorsport events including Formula E racing on a modified version of the circuit.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco spans 3. 337 kilometres through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, weaving around Monaco's harbor. Though officially named after the principality itself, the track is popularly known as Monte Carlo due to its location within that distinctive neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the resurrected Dutch Grand Prix beginning in 2021 before concluding its Formula One tenure in 2026. The venue, situated north of the seaside town of Zandvoort, returned the Netherlands to the sport's calendar after a lengthy absence.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km track featuring a main straight spanning 1. 068 km and holding an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his tragic death in 1977. The counterclockwise track hosts major racing events and features an associated kart facility honoring fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street circuit located along the Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, hosting the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural year in 2021.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown and Kallang districts, forming a temporary racing layout around the Marina Bay waterfront.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of racing capability. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile international-standard facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major motorcycle racing and endurance events, along with various touring car and rally competitions throughout its operational history.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championship titles from his 2005 and 2006 campaigns with Renault, along with 32 Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons. Beyond his single-seater success, Alonso has achieved significant accomplishments in endurance racing, including victories at Le Mans twice and winning the World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to excel in both Formula One and world-level sportscar competition.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes in Formula One competition. Since entering the championship in 2025, he has claimed eight Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He has achieved two runner-up finishes in the championship standings while with Mercedes and accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his racing tenure.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Alpine team. He represents his country in the sport's highest motorsport category.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan balances his endurance racing commitments in the LMP2 category with a reserve role at Haas, having made limited Formula One appearances during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri earlier in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian motorsport competitor who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France in international competition.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari, holding an unprecedented seven world championship titles that he shares with Michael Schumacher. He currently leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing extensive experience from his long career in the sport. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand-born racing driver, currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Racing Bulls team. Known for his competitive driving style, Lawson represents one of the newer generation of drivers on the grid.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc represents Monaco in Formula One competition with Ferrari, the Italian team. The driver achieved second place in the 2022 drivers' championship and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver who previously competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he races in the World Endurance Championship for BMW through WRT as a factory driver, while also taking on a part-time role in NASCAR's top series driving for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Over his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Earlier in his career, he achieved a notable victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after spending 15 seasons in the sport, during which he has secured six race victories. He achieved his highest championship finish as runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren, has secured nine Formula One victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following prior experience in IMSA's LMP2 division. His Formula One career spanned 2023 and 2024.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing in the sport's highest racing category.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, has transitioned to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing as a full-time Formula One participant from 2021 through 2025. He continues his involvement with the sport in a supporting capacity during the 2026 season.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian competitor, Verstappen drives for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag and has secured four consecutive world championship titles spanning 2021 to 2024. Across 12 seasons in Formula One, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver who currently holds a reserve position with Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport's top category between 2022 and 2024, representing a historic milestone as the sole Chinese-born driver to participate in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing operates from Enstone as Renault's factory team from 2021 onwards, adopted the Alpine marque to represent the French manufacturer's sports car division before Renault's planned exit at the conclusion of 2025. The squad inherited its facilities and infrastructure from the earlier Renault F1 Team era, maintaining continuity within the franchise under its rebranded identity.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through multiple organizational structures, with the current incarnation operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team designation.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari HP represents the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari in Formula One competition. As the sport's longest-standing and most accomplished team, Ferrari has participated continuously in the World Championship since its inaugural 1950 season, earning the popular nickname "the Prancing Horse" after their distinctive emblem.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American F1 team in 2014, with its racing program commencing in 2016. Currently led by team principal Ayao Komatsu following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, the outfit has competed under various title sponsorships throughout its existence in the sport.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering outfit was established in 1970 and built a reputation in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. After competing in the sport for over three decades, the organization departed in 2025 as one of the grid's longest-serving teams by race entries, subsequently being purchased by Audi to serve as the foundation for their F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited operates as a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking, Surrey, with its activities conducted through the McLaren Technology Centre facility. The organization functions as a subsidiary within the broader McLaren Group structure and is fully controlled by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: The Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, based in Brackley and holding a German racing licence, represents Mercedes-Benz's current involvement in Formula One, continuing a relationship with the sport dating back to 1954. From January 2022, the team operates under shared ownership between the Mercedes-Benz Group, Toto Wolff, and Ineos, each holding equal stakes. Mercedes-branded racing teams carry the historical moniker "Silver Arrows.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as Red Bull's second team alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team strategy in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that debuted in the 2024 season as the second constructor under Red Bull's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Operating from facilities in both Faenza and Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull GmbH's expansion within the sport's constructor grid.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian licence, has been a dominant force in Formula One since its 2005 establishment by Red Bull GmbH. The team, led by Christian Horner for two decades until his departure in 2025, is one of two F1 entries owned by the energy drink conglomerate, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following Williams's earlier failed F1 venture, is a British constructor based in Grove, Oxfordshire. The team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team banner.
